Article Title: 'Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother': Vijay moves Tamil anthem resolution; DMK, AIADMK back it
Article Text:
Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891. (Photo: PTI)

What does the resolution say?

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state.Moving the resolution in the state assembly, Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights and urged legislators to set aside political differences in supporting the measure."Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother," Vijay said in an emotive speech, adding that, "Tamil is not only a language but also our life and emotions.""Tamil means pride, Tamil means power. The moment you say 'Tamil', the entire Tamil Nadu will come together and stand as one," he said."Tamil Thai Vazhthu must hold the first place in Tamil Nadu. Giving first place to Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu is our state right," he noted."Saying that Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung first does not need to become a political debate," the Tamil nadu CM said, appealing to members across party lines to support the resolution.Under the resolution, Tamil Thai Vazhthu will be sung first at programmes held by educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in Tamil Nadu.The resolution received support from both DMK and AIADMK legislators, with members backing the government's move to mandate the singing of the state song at official functions.The move comes amid a recent advisory from the Union home ministry asking states and Union territories to comply with its January 28 directive on playing Vande Mataram before the National Anthem at official events.It also comes against the backdrop of a July 9 communication from the ministry of home affairs regarding the singing of state songs at official programmes.The resolution describes Tamil Thai Vazhthu as an expression of respect for the Tamil language and culture and links its mandatory rendition to the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed under the Constitution."Therefore, this House ( Tamil Nadu Assembly ) emphasises that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" is an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture. In accordance with the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India, and with a view to preserving the Cultural identity of Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly unanimously resolves that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" shall be mandatorily sung first, before the commencement of programmes held by all Educational Institutions, Universities, Government Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and other Public Institutions in Tamil Nadu," the resolution said.The resolution also notes that Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and describes Tamil civilisation as one of the world's oldest cultural traditions.Tamil Nadu had first directed that Tamil Thai Vazhthu be sung at the beginning of official functions through a government order issued on November 23, 1970.The state government formally accorded the song the status of the state song on December 12, 2021, making its rendition mandatory at official programmes and institutions across the state.Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state. Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights.

NEW DELHI: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The students, who have been agitating for 16 days, have announced a ‘Vidhan Sabha March’ despite the state government saying it has accepted 98 per cent of their demands.The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am, according to student leader Ravindra Paswan. He urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms.Speaking to ANI, Paswan said, "A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner. Students started gathering there at 9:00 AM. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 AM. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated. Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest; there will be a massive turnout."A prohibitory order has been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha from August 6 to 12.The restrictions will remain in force from 6 am to 10 pm each day.Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route to prevent demonstrators from reaching restricted areas.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyone’s responsibility. "We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.The Jharkhand Police and district administration have made elaborate security arrangements across the city ahead of the students’ ‘Vidhan Sabha March’. The government said no student would be harassed during the protest.Most schools in Ranchi will remain closed on Monday in view of the planned march, with authorities taking precautionary measures ahead of the expected turnout.The Ranchi district administration appealed to agitating students to refrain from aggressive demonstrations and cautioned against violence or illegal activities during the march to the Assembly.BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged that the party’s state unit president Aditya Sahu had been “put under house arrest” ahead of Monday’s protest.A prohibitory order was imposed in Jamshedpur from Sunday midnight in view of the protest march in Ranchi, according to an official statement.Protesters alleged that hundreds of students travelling to Ranchi from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by police forcefully.Student leader Ravindra Paswan urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms during the march, which is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana addressed concerns over a viral video that appeared to show a pellet gun, clarifying that the weapon was actually a paintball gun. "If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video--what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, colored balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun," he was quoted by ANI as saying.
Article Summary: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am. Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route.

BHUBANESWAR: Former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday described Gen Z as a force that cannot be ignored, saying he had told PM Narendra Modi that the responsibilities of an education minister were insignificant compared to the determination and aspirations of the country’s youth.Speaking in a light-hearted vein, the Sambalpur MP said he “suffered” because of Gen Z’s stubbornness but had come to realise that the new generation must be understood rather than resisted.Though some people tried to mislead Gen Z, Pradhan said, the ministerial position “was not at all a prestige issue for me”. Article Title: Jharkhand student protest: Govt to hold fresh talks as fasting student leader's health worsens
Article Text:
Jharkhand exam stir: Govt to hold fresh talks; health of student leader on fast deteriorates (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand government will hold another round of talks with protesting recruitment exam aspirants on Sunday, as the 16-day agitation continued and the health of student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike for nearly a week, deteriorated.The decision to hold a sixth round of talks came after discussions between the government and several student groups over Friday and Saturday failed to break the deadlock.Mahto's condition suddenly worsened around 3 am on Sunday at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Stadium, where students have been protesting since July 25. Doctors recorded his blood glucose level at 53.The government panel is scheduled to meet student representatives at noon on Sunday. The move, however, has drawn criticism from the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which has been leading the agitation.Ravindra Paswan, a leader of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accused the government of trying to divide the protesting students and divert attention from their demands."This is political manoeuvring by the government. It is trying to create a divide among students and divert attention. But they should know that all students are united," Paswan said at a press conference at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.Paswan claimed that the Reforms Manch had already presented its demands to the five-member government panel during a detailed meeting on Friday night. He alleged that the government subsequently held separate discussions with other student organisations that had not played a role in the ongoing protest.Govt says talks held in positive atmosphereThe Hemant Soren government held discussions with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch on Friday night, followed by four rounds of talks with different student groups on Saturday.The groups included the Congress-backed National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM) and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh (ACS).The government said the discussions were held in a positive atmosphere and that it was examining the concerns raised by the protesting aspirants.The decision to hold another round of talks was taken after the government panel met Chief Minister Hemant Soren for around four hours on Saturday evening.Rural Development Minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the panel briefed the chief minister about the demands raised by different student delegations."It was decided in the meeting with the chief minister that a final round of talks with the protesting students will take place at 12 pm on Sunday," she said.Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav said the government would continue discussions with students demanding comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).What are students demanding?The protesting students are seeking reforms in the recruitment examination system and action over alleged irregularities in various JPSC and JSSC examinations.The JCM submitted five demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination.The NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID investigation into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion within 90 days. It also demanded the establishment of a Jharkhand Testing Agency on the lines of the National Testing Agency.The ACS demanded that tribal and regional languages be included as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations. It also sought cancellation of examinations in which irregularities were found.Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had also issued an email ID through which aspirants could submit suggestions on reforms to the recruitment process.Protesters threaten Assembly marchDespite the government's talks with various student groups, protesters have said the agitation will continue until their demands are met.They have announced a march to the Jharkhand Assembly on August 10 if the government fails to address their demands by Sunday.The agitation has also seen the involvement of several student organisations, including the All India Students' Association (AISA) and Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).AISA set up a separate platform at the stadium on Saturday, although its leaders said it should not be viewed as a separate agitation.AISA national president Neha Bora, who was attacked with ink during Friday's Assembly march near Birsa Chowk, briefly joined the protest and raised slogans demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC and JSSC-CGL examinations.AISA's Ranchi unit chief Vijay Kumar said the organisation shared the same demands as the larger protest and that its members would join the August 10 march without carrying the AISA banner.The ABVP has also held protests over the issue. Its members scuffled with police on Friday while attempting to cross barricades near the chief minister's residence.Around eight to 10 ABVP protesters were detained during the march but were later released, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Ajay Aryan said.The ABVP has announced a separate march to the Assembly on August 11.19 arrested over alleged exam irregularitiesThe agitation comes amid an investigation into alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.Nineteen people have so far been arrested in connection with the case, while former JPSC panel chairperson L Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28.With the student leader's health deteriorating and protesters threatening another Assembly march, Sunday's talks could prove crucial in determining whether the 16-day agitation can be brought to an end or enters another phase of confrontation.
Article Summary: Jharkhand government to hold sixth round of talks with protesting students on Sunday. Health of student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike for nearly a week, has deteriorated. Students are seeking reforms in the recruitment examination system and action over alleged irregularities.

Article Title: 21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu MPs on Saturday "unanimously" decided to oppose Centre's Delimitation Bill after chief minister C Joseph Vijay chaired a meeting to discuss its likely impact on the state.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said around 21 out of 57 Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha MPs attended the meeting and agreed to resist any alteration in Tamil Nadu's representation in Parliament."The chief minister of Tamil Nadu had called for a meeting for all the MPs from Tamil Nadu from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. About 21 of us attended the meeting, and there was absolute unanimity that Tamil Nadu's rights must be preserved. Our representation in Parliament can't be diminished. Any kind of alteration and delimitation, either on the basis of population or on a proportionate increase, will be resisted," Chidambaram said."We want Parliament to be frozen at 543, and the distribution among the states to be preserved as it is, which means Tamil Nadu will have 39 members in a House of 543. We are clear in our unanimous opinion that a larger Parliament will be an ineffective Parliament, and Tamil Nadu will not be well served by a larger Parliament.So we want Parliament to be preserved at 543 with the same representation of 39 Lok Sabha MPs for Tamil Nadu," he added.The meeting was boycotted by the DMK and AIADMK, which dismissed the deliberations as a "farce" and a "drama".The meeting was held at Kalaivanar Arangam, a government-owned auditorium near the Secretariat.Read More : CM Vijay Tamil Anthem Resolution Senior DMK leader A Raja told reporters in Perambalur that it was "a farce, a laughable exercise", arguing that the TVK government was deliberating on an issue about which it had no clarity.Meanwhile, AIADMK called the meeting a "hurriedly staged drama", pointing out that no new delimitation Bill had been introduced in Parliament and there had been no official announcement on the exercise.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise. The opposition has demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament. However, its implementation has not moved forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.The Bill linked the implementation of 33 percent women's reservation in legislatures to delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu MPs "unanimously" decided to oppose Centre's Delimitation Bill. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay chaired a meeting to discuss its likely impact on the state. DMK and AIADMK dismissed the deliberations as a "farce" and a "drama"

Article Title: Government may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
Article Text:
The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies

Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill

NEW DELHI: The passage of FCRA amendment bill is not in Lok Sabha's agenda for Monday as Parliament's monsoon session enters its last week, giving rise to the view that government may be going slow on the contentious piece of legislation to sweeten the deal for parties such as DMK and NCP(SP), which are opposed to its provisions and are being seen by the governing alliance as prospective backers for its delimitation exercise.Sources said the meeting of LS's business advisory committee, where upcoming agenda items are finalised, on Monday will give more clarity as a schedule for discussion on the bill should be fixed if it has to be taken up for passage in the remaining four days of Parliament's monsoon session ending on Aug 13. Monday's agenda includes the introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill.The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments, saying it threatens their charitable works and will allow the government to seize their assets if their FCRA licence is withdrawn or not renewed.What has, though, made things politically trickier for the BJP is the support extended by DMK president M K Stalin to the demand of a delegation representing churches of different denominations in their meeting with home minister Amit Shah that the bill be either withdrawn or sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.With the government looking to assuage DMK’s concerns to get it on board before it makes a fresh bid for Parliament’s nod for its delimitation exercise, coupled with implementation of the women’s reservation law from 2029, it may not like to put the regional party on the defensive by bringing up the FCRA bill, some MPs said.Supriya Sule of NCP SP, another party being eyed by the government as a probable supporter for the amendment bill, has also opposed the FCRA bill.Mizoram CM Lalduhoma had told the media after joining a group of Church bodies from his state for a meeting with Amit Shah on Thursday that he was told that a debate on the bill is expected to be held on Aug 12.The continuing impasse in Parliament due to the opposition’s protests has added uncertainty as the government will prefer a full-fledged debate so that the home ministry could address the criticism around the bill.
Article Summary: Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill. Monday's agenda includes introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill. Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments.

Article Title: Jharkhand govt to scrap JPSC exams, rejects CGL cancellation demand; students vow to intensify stir
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: After holding a meeting with a delegation of protesting students, the Jharkhand government on Sunday agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC, JPSC Backlog 2023, and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams but rejected the demand to scrap the CGL examination, saying it was conducted under court orders and selected candidates are already employed.Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu said the government had agreed to "98 percent" of the points raised by the protesting students and decided to address the alleged irregularities through a "two-pronged approach".He said the criminal aspects associated with the 14th JPSC examination would be investigated by the CID and the Enforcement Directorate would be requested to probe alleged illicit financial transactions."Following three days of talks and extensive consultations, and acting on the instructions of CM Hemant Soren, the government decided to address the irregularities associated with the 14th JPSC and the 2023-25 backlog recruitments through a two-pronged approach. Criminal aspects will be investigated by the CID; furthermore, given the financial implications and evidence of illicit financial transactions, a request will be made for an ED investigation," the minister said."Following these discussions, student representatives demanded the cancellation of the CGL examination. The government clearly stated that, as the examination was conducted in accordance with the directives of the High Court and the Supreme Court, and is currently under their monitoring, it lacks the authority to cancel it. The government offered to oversee the investigation by constituting a monitoring committee headed by a retired judge; however, the students refused to accept this proposal. We believe the government agreed to 98 percent of the points raised," he added."The remaining two percent, specifically the demand to cancel the CGL exam, could not be met because the government cannot unilaterally cancel an exam conducted under court orders, where results have been published and successful candidates are already employed. To instill confidence among the students, the government was willing to form a committee headed by a retired judge to oversee the CID's work, thereby providing a channel for students to voice their concerns if they felt the CID was not listening to them. Overall, after these processes and efforts, we believe the government demonstrated genuine goodwill and sensitivity toward the students in its attempt to bring the agitation to a close," he further said.Meanwhile, the protesters maintained that their agitation would continue and that a march to the Vidhan Sabha would be held on August 10 until the case is transferred to the CBI."Let me clarify that our Vidhan Sabha gherao will continue peacefully. Our demand is for a CBI inquiry; we will not compromise on that," Kunal, a student leader, said."This was the second round of talks with the government delegation. Regarding the specifics, particularly the 14th JPSC, JPSC Backlog 2023 and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams, the government has decided to consider cancelling all three. Furthermore, the government has proposed CID and ED investigations into all exams conducted by the TDPL agency. Additionally, the government has accepted almost all of our demands concerning reforms, with the exception of one or two issues, such as age relaxation, on which no consensus could be reached."Regarding the CGL exam, the students demanded a CBI inquiry; however, the government did not agree to this. Instead, the government stated that a judicial inquiry would be conducted under the chairmanship of a retired judge, and if financial irregularities are detected, the ED would also be involved. Nevertheless, we students continue to demand a CBI inquiry," Ravindra Paswan, another student leader, said."The agitation will continue; the agitation is still ongoing," he added.The protesting students are seeking reforms in the recruitment examination system and action over alleged irregularities in various JPSC and JSSC examinations.The JCM submitted five demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination.The NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID investigation into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion within 90 days. It also demanded the establishment of a Jharkhand Testing Agency on the lines of the National Testing Agency.The ACS demanded that tribal and regional languages be included as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations. It also sought cancellation of examinations in which irregularities were found.Meanwhile, 19 people have so far been arrested in connection with the case, while former JPSC panel chairperson L Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28.
Article Summary: Jharkhand government agrees to address alleged irregularities through a "two- pronged approach" Minister says criminal aspects associated with the 14th JPSC examination will be investigated by the CID and the Enforcement Directorate will be requested to probe alleged illicit financial transactions.

Article Title: Police search 26 locations tied to banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K
Article Text:
Sopore Police conducts searches at 26 locations in UAPA case against Jamaat-e-Islami

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Police searched 26 locations across Sopore in north Kashmir on Sunday in a coordinated crackdown on banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K, seizing documents, literature and electronic devices as part of a probe into its alleged links to terrorist outfits and youth radicalisation.The search targeted residential and other premises linked to Jamaat-e-Islami J&K members and activists. No arrest was reported till filing of this report. “The operation was conducted in accordance with due legal procedure and prescribed protocols,” police said.Police said the seized material was being examined to establish further linkages and activities connected with the proscribed organisation. The operation was part of efforts to dismantle networks linked to banned organisations, separatist activities and terrorist funding.Distinct from Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Jamaat-e-Islami J&K has a history tied to regional separatism and has long had a support base in Sopore. Union government first declared it an “unlawful association” in Feb 2019 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. In Feb 2024, the ban was extended for five years, with the government saying the organisation continued activities against India’s security, integrity and sovereignty.Multiple criminal cases have been registered against Jamaat-e-Islami J&K and its members under various laws, including UAPA.Sunday’s search followed a sweeping crackdown in Kashmir after the fatal shooting of a J&K police head constable on duty in Anantnag town on July 22 — the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre in April 2025. Security forces demolished the family homes of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists and detained more than 2,500 people for questioning across Kashmir.
Article Summary: Sopore Police conducts searches at 26 locations in UAPA case against Jamaat-e- Islami J&K. Police seize documents, literature and electronic devices as part of a probe into its alleged links to terrorist outfits. No arrest was reported till filing of this report.

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Police on Sunday said it was prepared for the planned Assembly march by JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi, assuring protesters that they would not face action if the demonstration remained peaceful.The assurance came hours after a second round of talks between student representatives and the state government, with the administration agreeing to consider some of their key demands but failing to resolve the issue of a CBI probe into the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said adequate security arrangements were being made as a large number of students are expected to participate in Monday’s “Vidhan Sabha gherao”.“Precautionary force deployment will be carried out effectively; the Ranchi Police is fully prepared. There will be a large number of students. Instructions have been issued to all Ranchi Police personnel that if the protesters conduct themselves peacefully, no inconvenience will be caused to anyone,” Rana said.“However, if anyone attempts to resort to violence, appropriate legal action will be taken against them,” he added.Rana also clarified a controversy surrounding a viral video that appeared to show security personnel carrying a pellet gun.“If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video - what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, coloured balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun,” he said.The police officer said any pellet gun, if deployed, would be kept strictly for emergency situations.Meanwhile, student leader Ravindra Paswan said the government had agreed to consider cancelling three examinations - the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, JPSC Backlog 2023 and JPSC Backlog 2025.Student are set march towards the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha on Monday after government agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC, JPSC Backlog 2023, and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams but rejected the demand to scrap the CGL examination, saying it was conducted under court orders and selected candidates are already employed.On the CGL examination, students demanded a CBI investigation into alleged irregularities. The government instead proposed a judicial inquiry headed by a retired judge.Student leader Kunal said the “Vidhan Sabha gherao” would be held peacefully but maintained that the demand for a CBI inquiry into the CGL examination remained non-negotiable.“Let me clarify that our Vidhan Sabha gherao will continue peacefully. Our demand is for a CBI inquiry; we will not compromise on that,” Kunal said.The students have been protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations and are demanding accountability and reforms in the examination process.
Article Summary: JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi are set to march towards the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha on Monday. The students have been protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations. Government agreed to consider cancelling three examinations but rejected the demand to scrap the CGL examination.

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee on Sunday accused the BJP of being behind an alleged attack on former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee 's vehicle, after stones and other objects were reportedly hurled at her car in North 24 Parganas.Mamata Banerjee was travelling to meet the family of a TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody when the incident took place. TMC MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Dola Sen were accompanying her.Kalyan Banerjee described the incident as an "attempt to murder" and alleged that the attack was targeted at Mamata Banerjee. He also accused the police of remaining silent spectators while the incident took place."The entire car, there was not a single second when stones were not thrown. Stones were thrown every moment, targeting Mamata Banerjee to assault her," Kalyan Banerjee said, as cited by news agency ANI.He alleged that hundreds of BJP workers were present at the spot and claimed that the incident took place in the presence of police personnel."Hundreds and hundreds of BJP workers were there, and police were remaining silent spectators, absolutely silent spectators," he said.Kalyan Banerjee also alleged that there was a direction from West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari behind the incident."Of course there was a direction given by the CM Suvendu Adhikari," he said.TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee also accused the BJP of unleashing political violence in West Bengal and alleged that Mamata Banerjee was "brutally attacked" while travelling to meet the family of the deceased party worker.In a post on social media, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that the incident reflected a wider law-and-order failure in the state."And now, a former Chief Minister of the state, who was on her way to meet the grieving family, is brutally attacked by goons planted by BJP," he said, as reported by ANI.He questioned the police response and said the incident represented a "failure of governance"."This is not merely a failure of the state police. This is a failure of governance," Abhishek Banerjee said.He also alleged that the police had failed to protect TMC workers and the grieving family, and questioned whether political violence had become a tool of governance in the state.Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said Mamata Banerjee had gone to meet the family of the TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody and questioned whether she should have been prevented from making the visit."Our worker died in police custody, an incident akin to a lockup death. His wife is a councillor. You tell me, as a matter of simple, natural justice, should our leader, Mamata Banerjee, not go to meet that family?" Sen said.She alleged that stones and half-bricks were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle and claimed that BJP workers and police personnel were present at the spot."They attacked her in a targeted manner... BJP goons and police stood in front, throwing half-bricks and stones, cracking the glass of Didi's car," she alleged.Sen also said Mamata Banerjee's visit was not a political programme but an attempt to meet the family of the deceased worker.Mamata Banerjee herself alleged that large stones were hurled at her car in front of police personnel and said the attack could have resulted in serious injuries or death."Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements, right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open. We could have all been killed," she said.She also alleged that the police were providing protection to the BJP and said she had never witnessed such an incident before."This happened right in front of the police. I have never seen anything like this. What is going on?" she said."Chor bhagao" slogans were also heard from the crowd, according to ANI.West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya denied any BJP involvement in the alleged attack and condemned the throwing of stones or other objects at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle."Let me be clear: the BJP has absolutely no connection to the incidents where mud, stones, or slippers were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle," Bhattacharya said, according to ANI.He said the BJP did not endorse such behaviour and called for police action against those responsible."It is between the public and TMC," he said, while maintaining that the BJP condemned the incident.State minister Agnimitra Paul also condemned the alleged attack and said neither she nor the BJP supported such actions."Mamata Banerjee may have committed many wrongs or made many mistakes, but we can never support this kind of behaviour, especially against a woman, and an elderly woman. We do not endorse this. If anyone is carrying out such acts while claiming to represent the BJP, they are in the wrong," Paul said.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday stepped up its opposition to the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, with AICC general secretary KC Venugopal warning that the party and other opposition parties would strongly protest if the legislation is introduced in Parliament.Venugopal, speaking to reporters in Alappuzha, alleged that the proposed legislation was aimed at targeting minorities and NGOs and said the Opposition would not allow it to be passed."If the Central Government thinks they can cook up and introduce the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill within these two or three days, they should keep that wish to themselves," Venugopal said.He described the proposed legislation as "unconstitutional and anti-people", adding, "We will not allow such an anti-people and unconstitutional bill to be passed."The FCRA Amendment Bill, which seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, is expected to be taken up in the final week of the Monsoon Session.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also said on Saturday that the party would oppose the measure and that its strategy would be discussed at a meeting of Opposition floor leaders on Monday.Venugopal also sought answers from Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged use of force against students protesting in Delhi against irregularities in competitive examinations.He asked Shah to respond to allegations concerning the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas during the protests, and questioned his absence from Parliament."When students in India ask the crucial question of who ordered the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas shells against them to suppress their protest, Amit Shah would not come forward to answer it," Venugopal said.His remarks came amid a broader opposition campaign over the July 20 protests in Delhi, during which student protesters have alleged excessive use of force.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had also raised the issue during an interaction with protesters earlier.The Congress' opposition to the FCRA Bill comes ahead of the final three days of the Monsoon Session, with the party issuing a whip asking its MPs to remain present in both Houses on August 10, 11 and 12.Congress chief whip in the Rajya Sabha Jairam Ramesh said the party wanted to ensure that "history should not repeat itself", recalling the suspension of 146 Opposition MPs during the 2023 Winter Session.Ramesh said that after the suspensions, several major pieces of legislation, including the three new criminal laws, were passed with minimal Opposition presence.The Congress has also asked its INDIA bloc allies to ensure their MPs remain present during the final days of the session.The FCRA Bill requires a simple majority for passage, while any Constitution amendment bill on delimitation would require a two-thirds majority, according to the background information provided by the party.Venugopal also questioned the proposed restrictions on organisations receiving foreign contributions and raised the issue of foreign funding received by organisations associated with the RSS."If you have the courage, try controlling the RSS," he said.He also opposed the proposed delimitation legislation, arguing that it could disadvantage states that had successfully implemented population-control measures."This bill effectively chokes states that have successfully implemented population control," Venugopal said, referring to the proposed legislation.On the FCRA Bill, several Opposition parties have expressed concerns. NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule has called for the legislation to either be withdrawn or referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, while DMK president MK Stalin has also urged the Centre to withdraw it.The proposed FCRA legislation has also drawn regional concerns. Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma said after meeting Shah that he had raised six issues concerning the Bill and received an assurance that the legislation would not be retrospective.Venugopal further criticised the Kerala Police over an alleged defamatory statement by RSS ideologue T G Mohandas concerning the protests, saying an FIR should be followed by an investigation and appropriate action.
Article Summary: Congress steps up opposition to proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. AICC general secretary KC Venugopal warns that the party and other opposition parties would strongly protest if the legislation is introduced in Parliament. He asks Union home minister Amit Shah to respond to allegations concerning the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas.

NEW DELHI: Congress president and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi respond in Parliament to allegations of embezzlement of donations and missing valuables linked to the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya Kharge said the issue concerns the faith of devotees and claimed the Prime Minister should explain the functioning of the temple trust.Speaking to ANI in Rudrapur, Kharge said the opposition had raised the issue on behalf of people who have faith in the temple and Lord Ram."We were the first to raise the issue of theft of the assets inside the temple... Who appointed that trust of caretakers? It was our Prime Minister. Who inaugurated it? He did. Who started the worship? He did. Who hoisted the flag at the Ram Mandir? He did. Who selected the trust members? He did. That is precisely why we want that, since he orchestrated everything, to come to the House and provide a reply," Kharge said.Kharge alleged that jewellery, gold, silver, money and other valuables kept inside the temple were among the assets in question. He also referred to allegations involving gold bricks and a gold Ramcharitmanas book.He questioned the composition and functioning of the trust responsible for the temple's affairs and sought an explanation from the Prime Minister over the allegations.Kharge said devotees who have faith in the Ram Temple and Lord Ram were distressed by the allegations and that the issue had affected their religious sentiments.He also said people expected opposition parties to raise the matter in Parliament and asserted that the Congress had taken up the issue on their behalf. The allegations are already under investigation.The Uttar Pradesh government told the Supreme Court on July 27 that it had constituted a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by Inspector General of Police Kiran S, to investigate the alleged embezzlement of donations made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to the information provided by ANI, eight accused have so far been arrested in connection with the case. Investigators are tracing the money trail to identify additional assets and alleged beneficiaries.Earlier, several Samajwadi Party MPs also raised the issue in the Parliament premises and displayed posters carrying the slogan "Chanda chor, gaddi chhod" (Donation thieves, step down).The allegations concern the handling of donations and other valuables associated with the Ram Temple, with the investigation continuing to establish the extent of the alleged financial irregularities and identify those responsible.During his Uttarakhand visit, Kharge also said the Congress would oppose the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill and that opposition parties would discuss their strategy at a meeting of floor leaders on Monday."We will oppose the FCRA-related move. We will take a decision (about strategy) tomorrow after a meeting of floor leaders," he said.The FCRA Amendment Bill is expected to be introduced in the Lok Sabha during the final week of the monsoon session. The proposed legislation seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, with the stated objective of increasing transparency and accountability in the regulation of foreign contributions.Several opposition parties have opposed the proposed amendments.Congress leader KC Venugopal had earlier said the party would "vehemently oppose" the Bill and that the government "cannot bulldoze this type of bill".Kharge is in Uttarakhand as part of the Congress' preparations for next year's Assembly elections. He said his visit was aimed at energising party workers and expressed confidence that the party would form the government in the state."I am the AICC President. I cannot come here every day, but our army is present here... Does PM Modi come here every day? Does Amit Shah come here? Does Nadda, even though he hails from this very region, come here? Does the new BJP President come here? We visit when and where it is necessary to energise our party workers. That does not mean we simply arrive and leave like tourists," he said.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge demands PM Modi's reply in Parliament over alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement. I have closely followed his work and I have never hidden our friendship," the Baramati MP told reporters.She said Kishor worked independently in his professional capacity and that it was his decision to choose whom he wanted to work with."Whether the Sunetra Pawar-led NCP wants to work with Prashant Kishor or not is their internal matter," Sule said.Her remarks came days after Kishor met Nationalist Congress Party chief and Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son, MP Parth Pawar.Sule also praised Kishor for his political work in Bihar, saying he had won a "very big battle" in Bankipur despite facing the BJP's formidable political machinery. She pointed to data showing that the BJP had performed poorly even at "the booth of its national president" where Nitin Nabin is registered as a voter."Given this situation, we should appreciate Prashant Kishor. He is hardworking and has worked with several political parties over the years," she said.Sule also drew a comparison with her own political base in Baramati, saying, "If we had been in power from the local level to Delhi, and if there had been a negative result in our own booth in Katewadi in Baramati, I would have felt that something was seriously wrong with me," she said.
Article Summary: NCP working president Supriya Sule backs Prashant Kishor, says Sunetra Pawar-led NCP’s choice is ‘internal matter’ Sule said KishOr worked independently in his professional capacity and that it was his decision to choose whom he wanted to work with.

Article Title: Tiranga Yatra: Patriotic marches held across UP, Haryana ahead of Independence Day
Article Text:
School students and local residents hold national flags during a 'Tiranga Yatra' rally taken out ahead of Independence Day, in Ranchi, Jharkhand. (PTI Photo)

Yatras held across states

Haryana combines Tiranga campaign with fitness drive

What is Har Ghar Tiranga?

NEW DELHI: Tiranga Yatras were held across several parts of the country on Sunday as political leaders and citizens joined marches carrying the Tricolour ahead of India's 80th Independence Day on August 15. The events were organised as part of the broader 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign, with participants paying tribute to freedom fighters and promoting the message of national unity and patriotism.From Lucknow and Kharagpur to Narnaul, the marches brought together political leaders, students, young people and citizens. Participants carried the national flag and raised patriotic slogans as part of events planned in the run-up to Independence Day.The celebrations are also being linked to the commemoration of 150 years of ' Vande Mataram ', with activities planned across states during the campaign period.In Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh chief Minister Yogi Adityanath participated in a Tiranga Yatra organised by the Bharatiya Janata Party. The march began from the chief minister's residence at 5, Kalidas Marg and proceeded towards the Vidhan Bhavan.Thousands of young people participated in the procession, carrying the Tricolour and raising slogans including "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram".Adityanath said the yatra was an expression of gratitude towards freedom fighters and martyrs and urged participants to maintain discipline during the march."This Tiranga Yatra is an expression of gratitude towards all those martyrs and a resolve to carry forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's mantra of 'nation first'," he said.He also urged people to participate in the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign and hoist the national flag at their homes with due respect.In Kharagpur, West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh participated in another Tiranga Yatra and said similar programmes would be organised across the state."The Tiranga Yatra is being held across Bengal, with the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign taking the national flag to every household... The programme has started today and will be held in other districts as well. A major event will take place in Kolkata on the 10th, with thousands of people expected to participate," Ghosh said.The West Bengal government has announced plans to distribute 70 lakh national flags across the state as part of the campaign. A major Tiranga rally is also scheduled in Kolkata on August 10.In Haryana's Narnaul, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini flagged off a state-level half marathon organised under the 'Haryana Uday Abhiyan' with the theme "Har Ghar Tiranga".The event combined the Independence Day campaign with a message on fitness and the need to tackle drug abuse among young people."Carrying this vision forward, we have taken the message of a drug-free Haryana to the masses through the 'Haryana Uday' initiative. Whether through marathons, cyclothons, Raahgiri events, or various public awareness programs, we are actively engaging lakhs of young people and citizens in this mass movement," Saini said.He also spoke about action against drug trafficking in the state, saying illegal assets worth approximately Rs 53 crore had been seized and 111 properties acquired through illicit means had been demolished.The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign was launched in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations. The initiative encourages citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes and develop a personal connection with the Tricolour.The campaign also seeks to honour the sacrifices of freedom fighters and strengthen the spirit of patriotism among citizens.This year's campaign includes Tiranga rallies and processions, exhibitions, concerts, bike and cycle rallies, tricolour lighting of important locations, decorations and Rangoli programmes.Special activities are also being organised under the theme "Tiranga Salute to the Spirit of Vande Mataram", along with the "Selfie with Tiranga" initiative.The National Flag will also be hoisted at households and government offices during the campaign period.With Independence Day approaching, more Tiranga Yatras and public programmes are expected to be held across states as part of the nationwide celebrations.
Article Summary: Tiranga Yatras were held across several parts of the country on Sunday. Political leaders and citizens joined marches carrying the Tricolour. The events were organised as part of the broader 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign. The campaign also seeks to honour the sacrifices of freedom fighters.

Article Title: Amit Shah presents President's Colour to Puducherry Police
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday presented the prestigious President’s Colours to the Puducherry Police in a glittering ceremony.

PUDUCHERRY: Union home minister Amit Shah presented the President's Colour to Puducherry Police on Sunday.Shah presented the honour to the Union Territory's uniformed force's Ensign Officer at an official event held at the Puducherry Armed Police Ground in neighbouring Gorimedu. Shah was accompanied by DGP Shalini Singh.Lt Governor K Kailashnathan and chief minister N Rangasamy, among others were present.President Droupadi Murmu had announced on May 8 the conferment of the honour (Nishaan) on Puducherry police in recognition of its "exceptional service, discipline and distinguished achievements".The President's Colour is the highest honour given to a military unit or police of a state or union territory.Past recipients of the honour include the Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard and various state police departments.
Article Summary: Shah presented the honour to the Union Territory's uniformed force's Ensign Officer at an official event held at the Puducherry Armed Police Ground in neighbouring Gorimedu. Article Title: 6 years after NDA exit, SAD backs delimitation push
Article Text:
Badal's announcement conveyed the government’s efforts to realign the numbers in its favour this time round, after a similar exercise was defeated in the last session by a joint opposition, which has since been considerably weakened

Government likely to bring back delimitation bill , but timing not clear yet

NEW DELHI: A day after his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Saturday reversed his party's earlier opposition to the rollout of the women's reservation law from 2029 with an increase in the Lok Sabha's strength by 50% and supported any fresh move to implement the two together, signalling the possibility of the govt reviving the Constitution amendment bill soon.Akali Dal had walked out of the BJP-led NDA government in September 2020, ending a 23-year-old alliance, due to the Centre's passage of the three farm bills. DMK, another opponent being eyed by the government as a potential supporter of its renewed bid, snubbed governing TVK's all-party meeting on delimitation. NDA is also banking on NCP(SP) to support the measure.While Sukhbir Singh Badal’s party has only one MP — his wife Harsimrat is a Lok Sabha member — his announcement conveyed the government’s efforts to realign the numbers in its favour this time round, after a similar exercise was defeated in the last session by a joint opposition, which has since been considerably weakened.While DMK called it a diversionary tactic and wondered why CM Vijay did not summon the meeting on a pressing issue like the Mekedatu dam row, the party clearly did not want to be part of an exercise to frame delimitation as damaging to the interests of the state, with TVK ally Congress up in arms against it.Developments in governing BJP-led NDA and opposition camps are a clear indication that the government is bringing back the bill, which will need two-thirds support in Parliament.Its timing, however, remains uncertain, with a section of lawmakers being of the view that Parliament can be summoned after Independence Day to debate it.The ongoing monsoon session is scheduled to end on Aug 13, leaving the government with not much time to pursue its ambitious agenda that seeks to raise Lok Sabha’s maximum strength from the existing 550 to 850.Sukhbir demanded implementation of one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies. He said, “SAD also demanded a fair and equitable delimitation.” Incidentally, his wife had made a fiery speech against a similar bill last time, flaying the government for linking reservation for women to delimitation.The changed political environment and the fact that the government may write into the new bill all the assurances it has made verbally may have persuaded his party and DMK to consider a rethink.NCP MP Supriya Sule had earlier suggested that if the bill proposes a rise in Lok Sabha seats of every state by an equal proportion, it would not create any problem, though she had added that they will be part of opposition consultations before making a final decision.
Article Summary: Government likely to bring back delimitation bill, but timing not clear yet. Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal reversed his party's earlier opposition to the rollout of the women's reservation law from 2029 with an increase in the Lok Sabha's strength by 50%. He also supported any fresh move to implement the two together.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt

Rahul Gandhi raises Ken-Betwa displacement issue

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.
Article Summary: Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken- Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.

Article Title: 'They don’t need a certificate from you': Priyanka hits back at RSS chief Bhagwat’s Gen Z outreach

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Friday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s recent remarks on Gen Z and Gen Alpha, saying young Indians do not need his “certificate” or endorsement.Speaking to reporters outside Parliament, the Congress general secretary and Wayanad MP said, “They don't need a certificate from RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat ji.”Priyanka also said home minister Amit Shah appeared to be 'afraid' and questioned his absence from Parliament. Referring to alleged police excesses against students protesting over the July 20 paper leak issue, she said Shah should "come, give a statement, what is the issue with that. Something wrong happened, so take responsibility."Her remarks came a day after Bhagwat interacted with members of Gen Z and Gen Alpha during a session at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) in Mumbai. The outreach has drawn criticism from Opposition leaders, who have questioned the RSS' engagement with younger generations.Priyanka Gandhi's remarks followed a wider political response to Bhagwat's interaction. Karnataka minister and Congress leader Priyank Kharge also criticised the RSS and BJP, alleging that changes in their language did not represent a change in their ideology.Kharge said the RSS and BJP were “desperately updating their vocabulary” but alleged that they continued to divide people, misguide young people and “dress up hatred in new packaging”.In a post on X, Kharge wrote, “RSS & BJP are desperately updating their vocabulary, but unfortunately, it won't update their ideology. The truth remains the same, dividing people, misguiding youth and dressing up hatred in new packaging. Same Sangh, just different slang.”However, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backed Mohan Bhagwat’s remarks, saying Gen Z protests were about rights and entitlements, not against the country. He said opposing a government is distinct from opposing the nation and can help correct mistakes, urging authorities to halt action against the protesting youth."Not a single thing they said was against the country. It was certainly against the country's government, and the good thing is that Mohan Bhagwat has acknowledged this distinction," Abdullah told ANI.Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Ram Gopal Yadav also criticised the BJP over Bhagwat's interaction with Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Yadav alleged that the ruling party turns to the RSS when it faces political pressure.Speaking to reporters, Yadav said, “As the BJP government is feeling challenged by Gen Z, should they send Mohan Bhagwat to handle the situation. Whenever they find themselves completely cornered, they turn to him, asking them to find a solution or speak on their behalf...”The Opposition's response comes as political parties increasingly seek to engage with younger voters and address concerns raised by Gen Z. Bhagwat's interaction with young participants has therefore become a point of political debate, with Congress and SP leaders using the outreach to question the RSS' approach to India's youth.
Article Summary: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s recent remarks on Gen Z and Gen Alpha. She said young Indians do not need his ‘certificate’ or endorsement. Opposition leaders have questioned the RSS' engagement with younger generations.

Article Title: Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over its newly introduced social media law, alleging that it is aimed at silencing criticism of the government and reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's growing fear of public protests.Addressing supporters, former Delhi CM Kejriwal claimed the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours."The Modi government has introduced a new law. If the government asks any social media platform, whether Instagram, Facebook or any other platform, to delete a post or video, it will have to be removed within three hours," he said.He alleged that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption, while allowing abusive content from its supporters to remain online."If you speak against Modi ji, the government, paper leaks, the ethanol issue or corruption, your post will be deleted within three hours. But if people associated with them use abusive language or target women, no action is taken against such content," he alleged.AAP chief Kejriwal further claimed that Prime Minister Modi has become increasingly anxious after recent youth-led protests and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar."Modi ji fears the people of this country. He fears the youth, children and women. Ever since the protests at Jantar Mantar, he has been gripped by fear," Kejriwal alleged.Arguing that censorship cannot substitute governance, the former Delhi chief minister said silencing criticism would only deepen public resentment."The solution is not to silence people's voices. If the government does good work, people will praise it on their own. The public has no personal enmity with anyone. But if you suppress criticism instead of addressing people's concerns, public anger will only grow," he said.Kejriwal also warned that governments that fear their own citizens eventually lose public support."The days of a ruler who fears his own people are numbered. The more you try to suppress the voices of the people, the stronger their anger will become," he said.Earlier to this, Kejriwal also claimed that Meta restricted his account and slammed Mark Zuckerberg-led social media giant.

Article Title: Gujarat horror: PG girl raped on terrace; guard arrested
Article Text:
A security guard allegedly raped a 22-year-old student on a society terrace late Saturday





AHMEDABAD: A security guard allegedly restrained a 22-year-old student using a wire around her neck and raped her on the terrace of a society in Jodhpur late on Saturday night.Anandnagar police said the accused, Dharm Singh, 27, a native of Uttar Pradesh’s Hardoi district, was arrested from Hebatpur early on Sunday. He had been deployed at the society only six days ago.The woman, studying interior design in the city, was a paying guest in a flat in the society, and was on the terrace for a walk.The accused allegedly approached her with the intention of having sexual relations.Also read: ‘Maaf kardo’: Ahmedabad rape accused seen limping, repeatedly pleading for forgiveness in video When she refused, he allegedly assaulted her, restrained her with a wire around the neck and raped her.Police said the assault lasted nearly an hour. The wire prevented her from shouting for help. After he fled, taking her phone and locking her out on the terrace, she raised an alarm and was rescued by residents living on the floors below.She was taken to a hospital and police were informed.Sector 1 JCP Neeraj Badgujar said CCTV footage shows him taking the lift to the terrace around the time of the incident.Police said the accused had been deployed at the society for only about six days.He had worked for different security agencies for the past four years.DCP, Zone-7, Shivam Verma said while the woman’s medical condition is stable, she is under severe trauma.“She has been in the city for around two years for studies,” said Verma, adding that she tried to scream, but the accused had overpowered her and tried to strangle her with the wire.Police will next record her statement and probe if the guard knew of her routine.The security agency will also be questioned about his registration.
Article Summary: A security guard allegedly restrained a 22-year-old student using a wire around her neck and raped her on the terrace of a society in Jodhpur late on Saturday night. Police said the accused, Dharm Singh, 27, a native of Uttar Pradesh’s Hardoi district, was arrested from Hebatpur early on Sunday. The woman, studying interior design in the city, was a paying guest in a flat in the society.

Article Title: Karnataka activist Vatal Nagaraj calls for Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border blockade over Cauvery row

Karnataka activist Vatal Nagaraj announced a major protest on Monday





KRISHNAGIRI: Veteran Karnataka activist Vatal Nagaraj announced a major protest on Monday, stating that the Tamil Nadu–Karnataka border would be blocked to press demands related to the Cauvery water dispute and other issues concerning Karnataka’s welfare.According to his statement, the agitation was scheduled to begin at 11am near Attibele close to the Tamil Nadu State border, and was expected to affect cross-border transport and daily commuters.Following the announcement, officials confirmed that Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation buses operated from Hosur as usual."However, Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation buses did not enter Hosur since morning," a TNSTC official confirmed, adding, after 10am, the movement of Tamil Nadu buses into Karnataka would be reviewed depending on the situation at the border.The protest, led by Vatal Nagaraj, highlighted continuing tensions over Cauvery water sharing and the sensitivity of border districts such as Hosur, where transport and trade were closely linked to both states.

Article Title: No weekly offs, leave and workplace harassment: Mysuru woman dies by suicide, accuses manager
Article Text:
Nageshwari, 42, worked as a product promoter at a shopping mall.





MYSURU: A 42-year-old woman working as a product promoter at a shopping mall in west Mysuru allegedly died by suicide on Friday, accusing her manager of harassment.Vijayanagar police have booked the manager of a marketing agency on charges of abetment of suicide under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Nageshwari, a resident of Hinkal, left behind a suicide note in which she alleged that her manager, Dolly, who monitored her work from Bengaluru, harassed her by forcing her to admit to a mistake committed by someone else.She also claimed that Dolly continued to torment her by threatening to replace her with another employee and pressured her to resign from her job.Nageshwari, who had been working with the marketing agency for the past three years, further alleged that she was not given a weekly off after Dolly became her manager and was also denied leave.Her husband told police that about a month ago, his wife began complaining about Dolly's behaviour. He said that while he was away from home, she consumed a poisonous substance. Although she was rushed to a hospital, she succumbed late on Friday.Police said a case has been registered and an investigation is underway.
