Article Title: Strait of Hormuz standoff: What conditions have US, Iran set to reopen waterway
Article Text:
Iran says Hormuz will reopen only after US accepts its demands, while Washington seeks unrestricted commercial shipping. (Donald Trump, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian)

What Iran wants before reopening the strait

1. An end to US threats against Iran

2. An end to US military action

3. Withdrawal of US naval and air forces involved in the blockade

4. Compensation for damage caused during the conflict

5. Lifting of sanctions

6. Unfreezing Iranian assets

7. No US interference in regional negotiations

What Iran and Oman are negotiating

What the US wants

Washington also wants unrestricted commercial shipping

The US wants Iran to fulfil its commitments

Why the Iran-Oman deal is not enough

What could unlock the Strait of Hormuz

Pezeshkian signals room for negotiations

Iran has made clear that a deal with Oman on a new shipping arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz will not, by itself, reopen the strategic waterway. Tehran says the strait will reopen only after the United States accepts a broader set of Iranian conditions, while Washington has indicated that it is prepared to lift its blockade of Iranian ports once commercial shipping resumes without impediments.The competing positions have emerged as Iran and Oman move closer to an agreement on a new shipping protocol for the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow but critical maritime route through which a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments passed before the conflict.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran and Muscat were "very close" to an agreement on a new arrangement for shipping through the strait. However, he made clear that the agreement with Oman would not be sufficient on its own to reopen the waterway.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has also rejected suggestions that the reopening of the strait is simply a matter for the Iran-Oman negotiations.IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said the reopening of the waterway was "contingent upon the United States accepting Iran's conditions and has no connection to the Iran-Oman negotiations."He later said, "Whenever the United States accepts Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will certainly be reopened," according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.The statements point to a much broader dispute than the technical question of how ships will navigate the strait. At the centre of the disagreement are US military operations, sanctions, Iranian assets, compensation for wartime damage and control over shipping through one of the world's most important energy corridors.Iran's demands extend beyond an agreement with Oman on shipping arrangements. According to Al Jazeera, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has outlined several conditions for reopening the waterway.Tehran wants Washington to stop threatening Iran and end what it sees as continued US pressure against the country.For Iran, reopening the strait is therefore linked to the broader security situation. Tehran has argued that maritime arrangements cannot be separated from the military conflict and the wider confrontation with Washington.Iran wants the United States to halt military action against Iran and its regional allies.The demand comes after months of conflict involving US and Israeli attacks on Iran and Iranian retaliation against US interests and bases in the region.Tehran's position is that a return to normal commercial shipping must be accompanied by a wider reduction in military confrontation.Iran has also demanded the withdrawal of US naval and air forces involved in the blockade.The presence of US forces around the waterway has become a central point of contention. Washington has said it controls the blockade and has linked any lifting of restrictions to Iran meeting its commitments.US President Donald Trump said the US Navy was leading the blockade and that Washington controlled it."I don't want to say it has been... it's sort of open right now. We have a thing called the blockade headed up by the US Navy, and we control it. But they can always shoot something or drop a mine... if you have one mine sitting out there, you sort of mess things up because people don't want to take their billion-dollar boats and accidentally get hit by a mine. But I think we're doing very well. I am involved in the negotiations. I think we are doing fine... it could be soon."Another major Iranian demand is compensation from the US for damage caused during the conflict.Iran has indicated that an agreement on shipping cannot be separated from the economic and physical damage it says has resulted from the US military campaign.Araghchi has specifically said that US compensation to Iran would have to be addressed before the strait could reopen.Iran also wants US sanctions imposed on the country to be lifted.Sanctions have been one of the principal tools used by Washington to pressure Tehran. For Iran, their removal would represent a broader economic component of any agreement to end the confrontation.Tehran has also demanded that Iranian assets frozen under US sanctions be released.This would give Iran access to funds that have been restricted as part of the sanctions regime and would form another major element of the economic settlement Tehran is seeking.The IRGC has separately insisted that Washington must stop interfering in regional negotiations.Mohebbi said reopening the strait depended on "specific mechanisms and conditions" and was separate from the negotiations between Iran and Oman.This is important because Oman has been playing a role in discussions over the shipping arrangement. Iran appears to be treating the Oman talks as a mechanism for resolving the technical and legal aspects of maritime traffic, while insisting that the United States must separately meet its political and military conditions.Iran and Oman are working on a new arrangement governing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Araghchi said the previous shipping traffic separation scheme was no longer acceptable to Tehran. Iran is therefore discussing a temporary route with Oman while technical and legal questions surrounding a permanent route are resolved.The proposed arrangement is aimed at allowing commercial shipping to resume while addressing Iran's concerns over how vessels enter and leave the Persian Gulf.According to Reuters, a proposed deal could give Iran control over ships entering the Gulf through the strait. A senior Iranian source and two regional officials were cited as saying this would represent a major concession to Tehran.However, US officials have repeatedly indicated that Washington would not accept Iran controlling access to the world's most important energy trade route.This disagreement over who controls shipping is therefore one of the most difficult elements of the proposed arrangement.Washington's position is different from Tehran's.The US has indicated that it wants commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to resume without impediments and has tied the lifting of its blockade to Iran fulfilling its commitments.A US official told Reuters, "There is progress between Oman and Iran on the strait, and we expect a deal soon. Once the deal is announced to restore commercial shipping without impediments, the United States will lift the blockade of Iranian ports."The official added, "As always, US actions will continue to be performance-based and tied to Iran’s implementation of its commitments."This suggests that Washington sees the reopening of the strait as part of a reciprocal process. Iran would have to meet its commitments before the US takes corresponding steps.The US position centres on restoring normal commercial traffic through the waterway.Washington does not appear willing to accept an arrangement under which Iran has unrestricted authority to decide which ships can enter or leave the Persian Gulf.The issue is particularly important because the strait is a global energy chokepoint. Disruption there affects oil and gas shipments far beyond Iran and the Gulf region.Washington has also made clear that any concessions would be conditional.The US official said American actions would remain "performance-based", meaning Washington would expect Iran to implement agreed measures before the US follows through on its own commitments.Trump has also linked the broader negotiations to the US objective of preventing Iran from possessing a nuclear weapon.The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the wider Arabian Sea. Its strategic importance comes from the enormous volume of energy that passes through the narrow waterway.Before the conflict, the strait carried around a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments.That makes any prolonged disruption a global economic issue rather than simply a dispute between Iran and the US.When shipping is threatened, tanker operators face higher insurance costs, longer routes and the risk of vessels being attacked or detained. Energy prices can rise as traders anticipate shortages, adding to inflationary pressure.Iran's actions around the waterway have therefore attracted intense international attention.The UAE said on Saturday that Iran had attacked a carrier affiliated with its state oil company with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. No injuries were reported. Iranian authorities did not immediately comment on the allegation.Abu Dhabi National Oil Company has also said that 15 of its vessels had been struck while transiting the strait since the beginning of the conflict, resulting in one crew member being killed and 20 injured.The central problem is that Iran and the US appear to be negotiating different parts of the same crisis.Iran's position: A shipping agreement with Oman can resolve navigation and maritime arrangements, but the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Washington accepts Tehran's wider political, military and economic conditions.US position: Washington expects Iran and Oman to reach an arrangement allowing normal commercial shipping, after which the US would lift its blockade of Iranian ports, subject to Iran fulfilling its commitments.This creates a major gap between the two sides. For Iran, reopening the strait is part of a broader settlement with the United States.For Washington, reopening the waterway is more closely tied to Iran's implementation of commitments and the restoration of unrestricted commercial shipping.A deal would likely require progress on several issues at the same time.First, Iran and Oman would need to settle the technical and legal framework governing shipping. Tehran has said the previous traffic separation system is no longer acceptable and wants a temporary arrangement while a permanent system is negotiated.Second, Iran and the US would need to resolve the question of military activity around the waterway. Tehran wants US forces involved in the blockade withdrawn, while Washington wants assurances that commercial vessels can move safely without interference.Third, the two sides would have to address the economic issues raised by Iran, including compensation, sanctions and frozen Iranian assets.Finally, there would need to be agreement on who has authority over vessels using the strait. This could prove especially difficult if Washington opposes any arrangement that gives Tehran effective control over access to the waterway.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has indicated that Tehran sees an opportunity for diplomacy, even while maintaining that Iran will not surrender what it considers its rights.In a post on X, he said: "The best time to reach an agreement is the current situation. On the path to peace, we will not compromise on the rights of the Iranian nation. The government's main reliance is on domestic capacities and the people. The necessity of a compassionate approach toward the people | People are in two categories; either they are your religious brothers, or they are equal to you in creation."Pezeshkian's comments suggest that Iran remains open to negotiations, but Tehran sees the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as part of a wider agreement with the US.For Iran, reopening the strait depends on an end to US military action and threats, withdrawal of US forces involved in the blockade, compensation for wartime damage, lifting of sanctions, unfreezing of Iranian assets and an end to US interference in regional talks.The US, meanwhile, wants commercial shipping to resume without restrictions and expects Iran to fulfil its commitments before Washington takes further steps. It also opposes giving Iran unilateral control over the waterway.Oman is trying to help the two sides reach an agreement on shipping through the strait. However, Iran has made clear that an Iran-Oman deal alone will not be enough to reopen the waterway.
Article Summary: Iran says Hormuz will reopen only after US accepts its demands, while Washington seeks unrestricted commercial shipping. Iran and Oman move closer to an agreement on a new shipping protocol for the strait. Iran wants Washington to stop threatening Iran and end what it sees as continued US pressure against the country.

Article Title: Bulandshahr encounter: Wanted rape-murder accused carrying Rs 50,000 reward killed in police firing
Article Text:
The second suspect fled the scene, prompting a search operation, while a pistol, cartridges, spent casings and the motorcycle were recovered.





BULANDSHAHR: A wanted accused in the rape and murder of a minor girl was killed in a police encounter in Bulandshahr after two motorcycle-borne suspects allegedly opened fire at a police team during a checking operation.Senior superintendent of police Dinesh Kumar Singh said two police officers sustained injuries, while bullets struck the bulletproof jackets of two others."Today, a police encounter took place involving two motorcycle-borne miscreants. When the police signalled them to stop for a check, the miscreants--realising they were being cornered--opened fire directly at the police. One Sub-Inspector of the SWAT team and a Constable sustained injuries, while bullets struck the bulletproof jackets worn by two other officers. Assessing the situation, the police immediately returned fire in self-defence. One miscreant was critically injured in the police firing, while the other managed to escape," Dinesh told ANI.The second suspect fled the scene, prompting a search operation, while a pistol, cartridges, spent casings and the motorcycle were recovered."The injured miscreant was immediately rushed to the CHC. After receiving first aid, he was referred to the District Hospital, where doctors declared him dead during treatment. Upon verification, the deceased was identified as Monu. He was wanted for the heinous crime of raping and murdering a minor girl, and a reward of Rs 50,000 had been announced for his arrest. Multiple cases are registered against him...a pistol, spent casings, live cartridges, and a motorcycle used by the miscreants were found at the scene. ..combing teams have been deployed to locate the absconding miscreant, and a search operation is underway," SSP Kumar said.Further details are awaited.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A wanted accused in the rape and murder of a minor girl was killed in a police encounter in Bulandshahr. Two motorcycle-borne suspects allegedly opened fire at a police team during a checking operation. Two police officers sustained injuries, while bullets struck the bulletproof jackets of two others.

Article Title: ‘Hum don hain’: Student assaulted at Raipur school, video posted online with ‘Tirangaa’ dialogue
Article Text:
According to the complaint, the student was allegedly assaulted by fellow students, who are also accused of bringing outsiders to attack him.





RAIPUR: A video purportedly showing a student of the state-run Swami Atmanand School in the state capital being assaulted has gone viral on social media, raising questions over the safety of students on the school premises and the alleged inaction of the school authorities.According to the complaint, the student was allegedly assaulted by fellow students, who are also accused of bringing outsiders to attack him. The incident was reportedly recorded on video and uploaded on social media as a reel.The video allegedly carries dialogues from the film Tirangaa, including the threatening line, “Hum don hain, maa vakil hai, judge se setting hai” (I am a don, my mother is a lawyer and I have connections with the judge).The complainant further alleged that the mother of the accused student created a scene at the police station in an attempt to shield her son. Some lawyers also reportedly accompanied her in his support.The victim’s family approached the school authorities after the incident and complained to the principal. However, they alleged that no action was taken despite the complaint.Fearing further harassment, the victim subsequently obtained a transfer certificate (TC) from the school, according to the complaint.Purani Basti police said they had registered bailable offences against both parties.According to the police, the students, both of whom are in Class IX, had an argument over a disciplinary issue.Police said the video was posted by the student who was allegedly assaulting the other student and was deleted shortly afterwards.Cases have been registered against both parties under Sections 296, 115, 351, 327, 3 and 5 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), police said.
Article Summary: A video purportedly showing a student of the state-run Swami Atmanand School in the state capital has gone viral on social media. The video allegedly carries dialogues from the film Tirangaa, including the threatening line, “Hum don hain, maa vakil hai, judge se setting hai” (I am a don, my mother is a lawyer and I have connections with the judge) The victim’s family approached the school authorities after the incident and complained to the principal.

Article Title: Abdul Ghafoori arrested in murder of Indian-origin partner Himanshi Khurana in Toronto

Abdul Ghafoori charged with murder of Himanshi Khurana

Canadian police have arrested and charged a 32-year-old Toronto man with first-degree murder in the death of his Indian-origin partner, 30-year-old Himanshi Khurana , in December last year.Toronto police said officers from the fugitive squad and homicide unit worked with national and international law enforcement agencies to bring Abdul Ghafoori back to Canada. Article Title: French streamer Jean Pormanove’s shocking death takes another turn as two men are convicted over livestream violence
Article Text:
Jean Pormanove (Image via Instagram)

What happened to French streamer Jean Pormanove?

Why were Safine Hamadi and Owen Cenazandotti convicted?

The death of French streamer Raphaël Graven, known online as Jean Pormanove, has now led to convictions in France, bringing a major development in a case that raised difficult questions about online entertainment, consent and streamer safety. Safine Hamadi and Owen Cenazandotti were convicted over violence connected to Graven, who died during a livestream in August 2025. However, neither man was convicted of causing his death.Graven, 46, had built a large following by appearing in livestreams that frequently involved humiliation, verbal abuse and physical stunts. His content attracted more than one million followers across social media, with much of his audience watching on Kick.The streamer died in Contes, a village near Nice, in August 2025. His death occurred while his activities were being broadcast online, creating widespread concern over the nature of the content and the treatment he received during streams.French prosecutors did not pursue manslaughter charges against Hamadi and Cenazandotti. According to the prosecution, the probable causes of Graven's death appeared connected to his existing poor health and a fragile heart.The case nevertheless focused heavily on the violence surrounding his livestream appearances.Both men argued that Graven had consented to the stunts. His lawyer said Graven had previously told police that he agreed to the activities. The court ultimately acquitted the two men of abusing his psychological frailty.Although the court did not find them responsible for Graven's death, Hamadi and Cenazandotti were convicted of aggravated violence.Hamadi received an 18-month suspended prison sentence and a €5,000 fine. Cenazandotti was given a two-year suspended sentence and ordered to pay €15,000.Both men were also banned from posting on Kick for six months.The punishments underline the distinction at the heart of the case. The court found grounds to punish violence connected to Graven's treatment, while prosecutors did not establish that the defendants were responsible for his death.Hamadi expressed remorse during the trial, adding another emotional layer to a case that has drawn attention far beyond France.The controversy has also placed Kick under increased scrutiny. French authorities are continuing to investigate the streaming platform, although Kick was not a party to the proceedings against Hamadi and Cenazandotti.In a statement to the New York Times, Kick said: "The ruling relates solely to two individual content creators."That statement reflects one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding the case: how much responsibility should streaming platforms carry when extreme content becomes part of a creator's regular broadcasts?Graven's death has intensified debate about the limits of livestream entertainment. Content designed to shock can attract huge audiences, but the case has raised concerns about what happens when humiliation and violence become part of the business model.The livestream showing Graven after his death was later removed from Kick. His case now stands as a stark reminder of how quickly online entertainment can cross boundaries that are difficult to reverse.For his followers and the wider streaming community, the convictions offer some accountability. But with the investigation into Kick still continuing, questions about platform responsibility, consent and creator protection remain unresolved.
Article Summary: Raphaël Graven, known online as Jean Pormanove, died in August 2025. Safine Hamadi and Owen Cenazandotti were convicted over violence connected to Graven. Neither man was convicted of causing his death. Graven's death has intensified debate about the limits of livestream entertainment.

Article Title: 'We demand that NTA be dissolved': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka on CBI charge sheet in NEET 2026 case
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has demanded that the National Testing Agency (NTA) be dissolved and converted into a national technical testing commission following the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.“I just came to know that CBI has filed a chargesheet in the NEET 2026 case which involves a lot of NTA officers,” Ranka said.He also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEET-UG 2025 cases, and called for those responsible to be brought to justice.Ranka said the government should address what he described as structural problems affecting the country's examination system, including examination infrastructure and vendors involved in conducting exams.“It is imperative that the government takes steps to solve these structural issues that are plaguing the systems of this country, not just NTA but the entire exam system,” he said.“The exam infrastructure which includes the vendors have to be audited properly and it has to be made sure that the country doesn't see any more paper leaks,” he added.What does the CBI chargesheet allege?The CBI has alleged that the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak was part of a coordinated, multi-state conspiracy in which NTA-appointed subject experts allegedly accessed confidential examination papers and passed them on to middlemen and coaching operators for money.In a chargesheet filed before the special CBI court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue, the agency named 13 accused, including three NTA-appointed subject experts: Botany specialist Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, Chemistry expert Prahlad Vithalrao Kulkarni and Physics expert Manisha Sanjay Havaldar.According to the CBI, the leaked questions were circulated through a network of intermediaries before allegedly reaching candidates who paid for access to them.The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The agency alleged that forensic examination of seized mobile phones, pen drives and other electronic devices recovered PDF and image files containing NEET-UG 2026 questions.Investigators said the files were exchanged through Telegram, WhatsApp and other messaging platforms several days before the examination.The chargesheet names Tejas Shah, Shivraj Motegaonkar, Dr Manoj Shirure, Manisha Sanjay Waghmare, Dhananjay Lokhande, Shubham Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal in addition to the three NTA experts.The CBI has alleged that the accused played different roles in sourcing, circulating and distributing the leaked questions and handling financial transactions.The agency's investigation also included statements from candidates and their family members.In one instance, the CBI alleged that a candidate and her father were offered access to the NEET-UG 2026 question paper for Rs 4 lakh, along with coaching support and offline revision classes conducted by one of the NTA subject experts.The CBI said forensic evidence, chat records, recovered documents and witness statements support its allegations of criminal conspiracy, abuse of official position by public servants and illegal circulation of confidential examination material before the NEET-UG 2026 examination.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts. Ranka also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEet-UG 2025 cases.

Article Title: US appeals court halts Trump's $400 million ballroom project, grants 14 days for Supreme Court appeal
Article Text:
A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House (AP image)

A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House, dealing a significant setback to the president's plan to reshape the historic complex.In a 2-1 ruling, the Washington-based US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which challenged the project after the administration demolished the White House's East Wing and began building a 90,000-square-foot ballroom without congressional approval, cites Reuters.The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.The ruling comes after US District Judge Richard Leon had twice blocked above-ground construction while allowing underground work to continue. Leon ruled that "no federal statute comes close to giving the President" the authority to construct the ballroom without approval from Congress.The Trump administration has defended the project, saying the ballroom is needed to host large formal events while improving security at the White House.The ballroom is among several initiatives by Trump aimed at reshaping government buildings and national landmarks in Washington.During arguments before the appeals court in June, Justice Department lawyer Yaakov Roth argued that the judiciary had no role in reviewing the privately funded project."The courts have no role" in weighing the project, Roth said, adding that the preservation group's "architectural preference" against the ballroom should not outweigh national security concerns. He argued the former East Wing left "the president and others in the White House vulnerable to attack."Opposing the administration, Thaddeus Heuer, counsel for the National Trust for Historic Preservation, said the issue was not aesthetics but legal procedure. "They just don't want to go to Congress," Heuer told the court.Trump has repeatedly defended the ballroom and its rising cost, which has nearly doubled from initial estimates. In a post on Truth Social last month, he said the price increased because "it is approximately twice the size, and a far higher quality, than the original proposal," adding that "it will be magnificent, safe, and secure!"The ballroom case follows another recent legal setback for the administration after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been unlawfully added to the exterior of the Kennedy Center and ordered its removal.
Article Summary: A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House. In a 2-1 ruling, the court upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation. The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district, died in the blast. He worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.
